name: Nicotinamide
short: An overview linked niacin and nicotinamide to gut upset, liver dysfunction and flushing, nicotinamide less often. Pooled trials: more digestive effects; one 386-person trial: no noteworthy difference.
text: An overview of 14 reviews found that oral niacin and nicotinamide were associated with adverse effects including gastrointestinal upset, liver dysfunction, flushing, skin rash and fatigue, that nicotinamide had a lower incidence of adverse effects than niacin, and that effects were more common at higher doses and mostly resolved on dose reduction or stopping; tolerability was limited in people with conditions such as renal dysfunction, and the authors suggested regular monitoring may not be needed at doses under 1500 mg a day. A systematic review and meta-analysis undertaken to evaluate nicotinamide for the prevention of skin cancers, which included 29 randomised trials (3039 patients), found that nicotinamide was associated with an increased risk of digestive adverse effects. In contrast, a 12-month placebo-controlled trial of 500 mg twice daily in 386 participants who had had at least two non-melanoma skin cancers in the previous 5 years found no noteworthy between-group differences in the number or types of adverse events. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
